headline: Highest risk is medium: Dify can write and egress broadly while Pipecat routes shared-bus, multi-instance audio/text workflows, creating plausible prompt, leakage, and conflict paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and call APIs, while Pipecat runs on a shared bus with text/conversation state. That creates a plausible bridge where Dify-produced content can be consumed by Pipecat as instructions or context. No direct provenance controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are forwarded into Pipecat conversation state or bus messages
IF Pipecat parses shared-bus text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Dify message before bus publication
Disable automatic instruction-following on Pipecat bus inputs
Route Dify output through a human review step for control messages
Separate control and content channels in the bus
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs and can write/read the filesystem; Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state on a shared bus. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive content can flow between them. The profiles do not show isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Dify knowledge-base files or logs are exposed on the same workspace or bus as Pipecat
IF Pipecat forwards shared-bus content to external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Restrict shared-bus topics to non-sensitive metadata
Move Dify files and logs to a separate workspace
Turn off Pipecat forwarding for sensitive channels
Rotate and scope provider credentials per agent
requires-engineering: add per-message access controls and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad network egress plus filesystem write, and Pipecat supports shared-bus multi-instance operation. Even without explicit write overlap on the same directory, both can mutate shared conversation state or downstream resources, so coordination bugs are plausible. Lack of locking details means uncertainty should not be downgraded.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared workspace, bus, or downstream resource
IF no external lock or lease is enforced around shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use per-agent resource namespaces
Disable concurrent writes to shared state
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can emit tool outputs, and Pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework that can consume conversation state. If Pipecat treats Dify output as authoritative, errors can cascade into spoken or acted-upon responses. The profiles do not document verification gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Dify-generated text as authoritative conversation state
IF downstream actions or speech are triggered without verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat acts on Dify output
Require citations or structured fields from Dify
Limit Dify output to suggestions, not commands
Log and review high-impact turns
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and policy checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs, while Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if the same regulated data class is processed by both. No certifications or DPA details are provided, so uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed by both agents
IF their retention, residency, or logging policies differ for that data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable analytics on regulated streams
Align retention settings across both systems
Document residency for each provider call
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
